content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant**: Tomato plants, pulled from soil and laid out for examination
- **Affected parts**: Main stems prominently, with whole-plant collapse; roots visible
- **Key features**:
  - Extensive **bleaching/whitening** of the stem tissue, extending from base upward along major stems
  - Complete **plant wilt and collapse** — leaves drooping and dying
  - Pale tan-to-white stem cortex, desiccated appearance
  - Some darker lesions/cankers visible on the bleached stem surface
  - Root system appears damaged/brown
  - Foliage showing marginal browning and yellowing

**Differential Reasoning:**

- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot**: Causes characteristic pale/bleached stem tissue death, stem collapse, and whole-plant wilt. Stems become white and papery. Black sclerotia may form inside hollow stems (may not be visible externally). The extensive stem bleaching running well up the main stem is classic.
- **Southern Blight**: Also bleaches stems, but damage is typically confined to the soil-line region. The bleaching here extends higher on the stems.
- **Verticillium Wilt**: Internal vascular browning, V-shaped leaf yellowing — the exterior stem bleaching visible here is not characteristic.
- **Bacterial Wilt / Bacterial Canker**: No visible white/bleached stem tissue; typically causes vascular discoloration and ooze.

The extensive **stem bleaching extending up from the base**, combined with **total plant collapse**, most strongly matches **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*), where the fungus kills and bleaches stem tissue, causing the plant to die back from the inside out.
